transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 11:00 PT / 14:00 ET
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (BlueWave), Michael Park (BlueWave Infra), Sara Li (BlueWave PM)

---- Auto-generated Summary (may be rough) ----
High-level: onboarding progressing, need to clear KMS perms and service account TTL, staging KV cache mismatch causing higher p99, plan a limited canary once sweep looks good.

[00:00] Liam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, and then we'll go through access, bench numbers, and the canary plan. uh Priya do you want to kick off with the bench highlights?
[00:18] Priya Shah: Yeah sure. thanks Liam. so I ran the first batch of runs yesterday in staging with the same model config you gave us — 8k context, 16-bit quant profile — and we saw median latency about 120ms per token with batching of 8. p95 was at 450ms, p99 spiked to around 1.2 seconds on two outliers.
[00:42] Dana Ortiz: Sorry can I clarify, that is per-token or per-request? our baseline is per-request at our app level.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Good question. that's per-token; per-request for your prompt set averaged 320ms median. there is some jitter because of cold-starts when the prefix cache is empty.
[01:05] Michael Park: When you say prefix cache, you mean the KV cache? we've noticed some misses in staging, we call that the kv cash in our logs, heh.
[01:13] Priya Shah: yeah, kv cache, kv cash, same thing — the prefix caching didn't warm for about 15% of the run which explains the p99 delta. we traced it to the gateway routing TTL — routing dropped some of the pre-warm calls.
[01:28] Liam Carter: okay so sounds like two threads: infra side (routing/TTL) and Redwood side (warm policy). Michael, any blockers on your end to increasing TTL for the pilot SA?
[01:40] Michael Park: We're fine to extend but need to know the expected rotation window. right now token TTL is 1 hour and rotates automatically, which hits the run every now and then. if we go to 8 hours for the pilot that should remove most of the rotation noise.
[01:54] Priya Shah: 8 hours would be perfect for the canary. and we'll instrument to ignore runs that coincide with rotation events.
[02:05] Sara Li: on the quality side, we saw a few regressions on hallucination metrics with the quantized profile — should we run a quick quality check with the 50-example set?
[02:14] Priya Shah: yes please. Dana, if you can drop the example prompts we'll run the regression tests alongside the latency sweep.
[02:22] Dana Ortiz: I'll upload them to the shared drive after this call.

[02:40] Liam Carter: Security — quick status. I sent a link to the SOC2 doc last week, but I heard we need the KMS notes and a short gist on HSM support?
[02:50] Dana Ortiz: our security team also wants to confirm we can bring our keys — we prefer customer-managed keys + access via our KMS.
[02:57] Priya Shah: Redwood Private supports that; for the hosted pilot we can integrate with your KMS via a service account and a key proxy. we'll send a one-page integration note — there might be a few IAM permissions we need from your side.
[03:10] Michael Park: will need exact permission list to get it routed through procurement.
[03:14] Liam Carter: we'll send that today.

[03:35] Priya Shah: back to perf, we also tried a dedicated pool run for one hour — throughput improved predictably, median tokens down to 95ms, but cost is higher. for this pilot you said you wanted to evaluate cost vs latency — is there a target latency band you care about?
[03:52] Dana Ortiz: ideally under 200ms per request at median for our user flows. p95 under 500ms would be great.
[03:58] Priya Shah: got it. with dedicated we can hit that easily, but with shared hosted configs we can get close with batching + prefix cache warm.
[04:10] Liam Carter: question for product — Sara, are you comfortable with a canary that ramps to 5% of traffic for 2 hours?
[04:17] Sara Li: yes that sounds fine, we just need the incident playbook and the rollback procedure documented. also a contact list for the run.
[04:25] Priya Shah: we'll include the runbook. rollback is immediate switch back to incumbent endpoint and then a short postmortem within 24 hours.

[05:00] (15:00–30:00 block of deeper troubleshooting and clarifications; transcription shows occasional overlaps)
[15:03] Michael Park: we found one more oddity: the gateway logs show 401s for about 7 calls in last night run — looks like short-lived SA keys failing.
[15:12] Priya Shah: that's probably the token rotation hitting during a long-run. we'll change our client to retry on transient auth failures and backoff.
[15:21] Dana Ortiz: is that safe for patient data? we have HIPAA concerns — retries could duplicate calls.
[15:28] Priya Shah: good call. for any health-related production traffic we won't do blind retries; instead we'll use idempotency keys and our client will dedupe. for the pilot bench runs it's okay to retry but we'll annotate duplicates in the results.

[22:40] Liam Carter: let's make sure the bench spreadsheet captures idempotent flags and which runs had retries. Priya can you add a column?
[22:47] Priya Shah: yes i'll add a "retries/idempotent" column and a note for any run with auth errors.

[24:12] Sara Li: about observability — do we get token-level cost breakdowns in the pilot? we need that to map spend to features.
[24:21] Liam Carter: yes, Redwood Console will give token, route, and model-level breakdowns. retention for the pilot is 30 days by default, we can extend as an add-on.
[24:33] Michael Park: can we push logs to our Splunk?
[24:36] Priya Shah: yes, we support pushing traces and logs to external sinks; we'll share the connector config. it may require a small NAT config change.

[30:00] (wrap-up section)
[30:12] Liam Carter: OK wrap. recap of blockers: Michael to extend SA TTL, Dana to upload prompt set, Priya to run latency sweep and add retries column, Liam to send KMS/SOC2 docs and book canary window.
[30:28] Dana Ortiz: quick question — is there any change in the rollback SLA if we do a private deployment vs hosted?
[30:35] Liam Carter: yes, private/on-prem has different operational SLAs; we'll include the difference in the doc but the rollback mechanics are the same — immediate endpoint switch + we keep logs to assist postmortem.
[30:47] Priya Shah: one more note: in dedicated mode we also recommend enabling the quant compensation profile to keep quality steady if you use 16-bit quant. that reduced our hallucination counts in tests.

[31:10] Sara Li: perfect. let's lock the canary date after the sweep.
[31:14] Liam Carter: agreed. i'll propose Tue/Wed next week, 2-hour windows.

[45:00] (end)

---- Explicit next steps (spoken recap) ----
- Priya to run latency sweep and update bench sheet (500 requests, include cold/warm starts) — Due Fri 6/18
- Liam to send SOC2 + KMS integration note and permissions list — Due Thu 6/17
- Michael to extend pilot SA token TTL to 8 hours — Due Tue 6/16
- Dana to upload 50 example prompts for quality regression — Due Fri 6/19
- Liam/Priya to schedule canary window and invite infra/product — Due Thu 6/17

Shared artifacts referenced during call: bench spreadsheet (link: drive.google.com/bluewave-poc-bench), SOC2 summary (link: drive.google.com/redwood-soc2), canary runbook (note: to be shared after call).

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings of technical terms (e.g., "KV cash" for "KV cache"), speaker attribution is best-effort.
